godavari.label: Kaleshwaram Lift Irrigation Scheme — Godavari system
godavari.summary: The world's largest multi-stage lift scheme: Godavari water is pumped roughly 500 m uphill in a chain of barrages, tunnels and pump houses to reach the Deccan plateau.

trunk.pumpNote: 17 × 40 MW = 680 MW · Kannepalli village near Medigadda · inaugurated Jun 2019 as the “world's biggest pumphouse” · barred from full operation since the Oct 2023 Medigadda pier subsidence, pending NDSA-directed repairs (targeted ~2027).
12 × 40 MW = 480 MW (some sources cite 8 units / 320 MW from an earlier commissioning snapshot) · under NDSA no-storage restriction since 2024.

14 × 40 MW = 560 MW · discharges ≈656 cusecs into Yellampally, the terminus of Kaleshwaram Link-1 · no separate ‘Yellampally pump house’ exists — this is the facility that fills it. Link-1 total: 43 units / 1,720 MW across Lakshmi+Saraswathi+Parvathi.

trunk.pumpFromPrev: Nandi Pump House → Gayatri Pump House (Ramadugu)
trunk.pumpNote: Nandi / Nandimedaram: 7×~124.5 MW = 871 MW, lift ≈105–110 m. Gayatri / Ramadugu (Lakshmipur village): 7×139 MW = 973 MW, lift 111 m — marketed as the world's largest underground pump house (4 floors, ~178 m below surface). Combined they lift Yellampally (148 m) water into Mid Manair Dam (318 m). Corrects this dataset's earlier ‘Ramadugu · Kannepalli · Gandhari’ label — Kannepalli is a real KLIS pump house but belongs to the separate Medigadda→Annaram leg, and no ‘Gandhari’ pump house could be confirmed in any source.
4 × 106 MW = 424 MW · near Ananthagiri, Illanthakunta mandal, Siddipet district.

4 × ~134–135 MW = ~538 MW. One source separately cites a 117 m lift for this station, which doesn't match the ~20 m single-hop figure used here — treat the lift height as unconfirmed pending a primary source.
8 × 43 MW = 344 MW · discharge ≈248.5 cumecs. A separately reported ‘18-machine’ Station-8 figure does not reconcile with this 8-unit total.

trunk.pumpFromPrev: Akkaram Pump House → Markook Pump House
trunk.pumpNote: Akkaram (Gajwel mandal): 6×27 MW = 162 MW — verified against this dataset's earlier figure. Markook (near Kondapochamma Sagar): 6×34 MW = 204 MW — previously missing from this dataset entirely. The ≈61 m lift is actually split across these two stations via an intermediate Markook surge pool; the exact per-station split is not confirmed.

branches.pumpNote: 3 × 132 MW = 396 MW · reached via a ~12 km tunnel from Narlapur to Regonda · verified correct against multiple sources. Feeds Gouravelli Reservoir (8.23 TMC, Gudatipally village, Akkannapet mandal), serving the Husnabad area.

totals.note: Government/press materials widely cite '618 m' as the total lift figure, but 618 m is Kondapochamma Sagar's absolute elevation above sea level — the cumulative lift from the Godavari at Medigadda works out closer to ~520-526 m.

krishna.label: Krishna system — predominantly gravity-fed
krishna.summary: From Jurala through Srisailam to Nagarjuna Sagar, Krishna water descends by gravity alone — no pumping on the main stem. Several large lift schemes branch off the Srisailam/Jurala foreshore to reach higher plateau land nearby.

liftSchemes.name: Kalwakurthy Lift Irrigation Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi KLIS)
liftSchemes.notes: 3 pumping stages (5×30 MW = 150 MW each, 450 MW total), 4 balancing reservoirs (Yellur, Singotam, Jonnalaboguda, Gudipally Gattu); command area ~3.4–3.65 lakh acres across Nagarkurnool, Wanaparthy, Mahbubnagar, Shamshabad. Reported total lift (298 m) doesn't exactly reconcile with the elevation gap (257.6 m) between the cited source/destination points — an unverified stage breakdown of 95+86+117=298 m is self-consistent but not confirmed against a primary document. Chronically under-utilised: typically only 3 of 5 pumps run per stage because the downstream canal's carrying capacity is well below the pumps' design discharge; integration with PRLIS has been proposed to fix this.

pumpHouses.name: Lift-III — Gudipally
pumpHouses.note: suffered a 2-day outage in Aug 2019 from a switching-system fault

liftSchemes.name: Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme
liftSchemes.notes: 5-stage pumping system designed to lift 90 TMC of monsoon floodwater over ~60 days into 6 reservoirs (Anjanagiri, Sri Veeranjaneya, Venkatadri + Kurumurthyraya, Udandapur, K.P. Lakshmidevipally); combined storage 67.52 TMC; command area 12.3 lakh acres. Design total ~4,720 MW (31×145 MW + 3×75 MW pumps, supplied by BHEL — larger than Kaleshwaram's 139 MW units). Phase I (Narlapur/Anjanagiri) inaugurated 16 Sep 2023; by Rabi 2025 Anjanagiri was fully operational with Veeranjaneya/Venkatadri partially irrigating. Cost escalated from ₹35,200 Cr to a projected ₹65,506 Cr; completion deadline pushed to Dec 2027. Stage V (K.P. Lakshmidevipally) is the least documented and least advanced stage.

pumpHouses.name: Stage II — Yedula (Edula)
pumpHouses.note: houses one of India's largest underground pump caverns (415 m × 30 m × 90 m); under construction, partially operational Rabi 2025

liftSchemes.name: Dindi Lift Irrigation Scheme (R. Vidyasagar Rao)
liftSchemes.sourceLabel: PRLIS's Sri Veeranjaneya (Yedula) Reservoir → Ulpara Barrage, gravity link
liftSchemes.notes: CORRECTED (Aug 2026 research): despite being called a ‘lift’ scheme, DLIS's own works have no pump house — they are a gravity cascade. The genuine ~175 m lift from Srisailam (270 m) up to Yedula Reservoir (445 m) is performed entirely by PRLIS's own Narlapur/Yedula pump houses, outside DLIS's scope; a 13.03.2024 government memo formally fixed DLIS's water-drawal point at PRLIS's Yedula Reservoir. From there, water reaches Ulpara Barrage (412 m) and flows by gravity through a 66.3 km main canal and 9 reservoirs (not 12, per the Irrigation Dept.'s own 2024 figures) down to Shivannagudem Balancing Reservoir (385.6 m, 155,000-acre command). Command area 3.61 lakh acres across 4 districts. Sanctioned 2015 (₹6,190 Cr); as of mid-2026 still under construction (only ~12,000 of 361,000 acres irrigated), stalled by land acquisition/R&R and an NGT/Supreme Court environmental-clearance dispute. Three small, unrelated lift schemes bundled under the same Irrigation Circle (Ambabhavani 2×4.5 MW, Kambalapally 2×3.5+2×2.5 MW, Pogilla 3×0.35 MW) draw separately from the Nagarjuna Sagar foreshore for local fluoride-affected villages — not part of the main 25.6 TMC DLIS network.

liftSchemes.name: Rajiv Bheema Lift Irrigation Scheme
liftSchemes.sourceLabel: Jurala (PJP) backwaters — two intakes: Panchadevpad (Lift-I) and Ookachettivagu pondage near Ramanpad (Lift-II)
liftSchemes.notes: Irrigates roughly 203,000 acres (111,000 under Lift-I + 92,000 under Lift-II) across Wanaparthy, Narayanpet and Nagarkurnool districts. Total installed capacity 119 MW across both lifts combined; per-stage unit counts and MW split are not documented in available sources. Administrative sanction ₹2,158.40 Cr; commissioning date not confirmed, implying a long-running, phased build typical of Krishna-basin lift schemes.

pumpHouses.name: Lift-I — Panchadevpad
pumpHouses.note: Jurala/PJP foreshore intake; unit count and per-stage MW not found in available sources

pumpHouses.name: Lift-II — Ramanpad / Kothakota (Ookachettivagu)
pumpHouses.note: draws from Ookachettivagu project pondage, not directly from Jurala; feeds Shankarasamudram balancing tank near Kanayapally village

liftSchemes.name: Jawahar Nettempadu Lift Irrigation Scheme (JNLIS)
liftSchemes.sourceLabel: Jurala (PJP) foreshore, near Upperu village, Dharur mandal
liftSchemes.notes: CORRECTED (Aug 2026 research): sourced from the Jurala backwaters, not Srisailam — this dataset previously and incorrectly grouped it among Srisailam-fed schemes. Two-stage lift (Upperu, then Relampadu/Marlabeedu near Dharur) feeding the Gudemdoddi (2.0 TMC) and Relampadu (2.3 TMC) balancing reservoirs — NOT Udandapur Reservoir, which this research confirms is actually PRLIS Stage IV (fed from Kurumurthyraya, ultimately from Srisailam). Command area ~2 lakh acres across 148 villages in 8 mandals of Jogulamba Gadwal district; foundation laid 2015; partially operational since at least 2021 (only 2 of 4 Stage-I pumps running as of the last confirmed report, achieving ~1,789 of a 2,250-cusec target).

pumpHouses.name: Stage I — Upperu
pumpHouses.note: unit MW figure (17 MW) is a single, unconfirmed aggregator source; only 2 of 4 pumps operational as of the last confirmed (2021) report

pumpHouses.name: Stage II — Relampadu / Marlabeedu
pumpHouses.note: at least 3 units per tender documents; feeds Relampadu Balancing Reservoir

dataNotes: Kaleshwaram's total lift is reported inconsistently: 618 m (Kondapochamma Sagar's elevation) vs ~520-526 m (computed cumulative lift from Medigadda). Both figures are shown; treat 618 m as elevation, not lift.
Kaleshwaram's official target capacity is 240 TMC (195 from Medigadda + 20 from SRSP diversion + 25 groundwater recharge) — a figure disputed by CAG audit and opposition sources.
Ananthagiri Reservoir's elevation (470 m) is interpolated between Mid Manair Dam and Ranganayaka Sagar — not independently confirmed.
Individual barrage capacities (e.g. Annaram: 10.87 vs 11.9 TMC) show minor inconsistencies across Wikipedia and news sources.

The Kalwakurthy scheme's reported total lift (298 m) does not arithmetically match its cited source/destination elevations (a 257.6 m gap) — likely reflects staging not captured by simple subtraction.

Map connector lines between reservoirs come in two kinds: solid lines follow a documented intake, canal or lift scheme (e.g. Kaleshwaram's offline chain, NSP left canal to Wyra/Palair, Srisailam/Jurala lift-scheme foreshores). Dashed lines (Kinnerasani, Laknavaram, Ramappa) connect a standalone tank to its nearest mapped hub purely for visual continuity and are not a claim about the actual engineered route.

Pump house research (Aug 2026, see research/ folder): Kaleshwaram Stage-1 (Lakshmi/Medigadda, Saraswathi/Annaram, Parvathi/Sundilla) totals 43 units / 1,720 MW, independently corroborated across two outlets — there is no separate fourth 'Yellampally pump house'; Parvathi's discharge is what fills Yellampally.

The Yellampally→Mid Manair leg is really the Nandi and Gayatri pump houses, not 'Ramadugu/Kannepalli/Gandhari' as this dataset previously modeled — 'Kannepalli' is a real KLIS pump house but belongs to the separate Medigadda→Annaram leg, and no 'Gandhari' pump house could be confirmed in any source.

Udandapur Reservoir is fed by the Palamuru-Rangareddy Lift Irrigation Scheme (via Kurumurthyraya), not by a Jurala→Udandapur 'Nettempadu' link as this dataset previously modeled in its map connections.
The Dindi Lift Irrigation Scheme has no pump house of its own — it is a gravity cascade fed from PRLIS's Yedula Reservoir; all lift from Srisailam is performed by PRLIS pump houses, not Dindi's.

All pump house names, unit counts and capacities are drawn from the research/ folder's per-scheme reports (Aug 2026). Several figures (unit counts, lift heights, discharge) vary across press sources and are flagged as uncertain within those reports — treat pump-level numbers as approximate, cross-checked estimates rather than official figures.
